notes: Identity verified: supplied canonical text has matching title Eighteen- and 24-month-old infants correct others in anticipation of action mistakes, authors Birgit Knudsen and Ulf Liszkowski, and DOI 10.1111/j.1467-7687.2011.01098.x. Full primary journal report includes methods, results, discussion and references. Header is Developmental Science 15:1 (2012), pp 113–122; input cites 2011, the copyright/acceptance year. No PDF supplied. Target unresolved: no numbered Study 1 heading disambiguates the input. Source p.6 (printed p.118) continues 18-month analyses and reports 24-month results. Description does not specify age, control contrast, mean points versus number of infants, or trial restriction. Candidates: 18-month mean-point planned one-tailed LSD comparisons, mistaken vs correct action Cohen’s d=.782, p=.005; mistaken vs different action Cohen’s d=.939, p=.002 (p.117). Omnibus F(2,45)=5.44, p=.008. At 24 months the within-subject mean-point comparison has t(15)=3.72, p=.001, Cohen’s d=.794; number-of-infants McNemar p=.035 (p.118). Other 18-month categorical candidates: Fisher exact both ps=.019; first-trial mistaken vs correct p=.086 and mistaken vs different p=.022. These are separate tests. Candidate participant N: 48 18-month-olds across three between-subject conditions, explicit denominators 16 per condition; 16+16=32 per pairwise contrast, 16+16+16=48 for all three. Explicit 24-month N=16 is within subjects; condition counts are not added. Seven 18-month and six 24-month exclusions (10 fussiness, two experimenter error, one parental interference) reported separately; no subtraction from participating groups. All sample counts remain candidates for parent field-scope review. No target chosen by numeric matching, metric matching or proximity. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
